svg.title: Lobster AI: how you call it, where it runs and what you get
svg.desc: Lobster AI runs on your machine: analysis runs there and data files stay there. You call it from the terminal (lobster chat, lobster query), from MCP hosts such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex and Cursor (lobster mcp --stdio), or from other programs (lobster agent --stdio, JSON Lines). The engine is a supervisor that routes each request to specialist agents from packages you install as needed: genomics, proteomics and transcriptomics are 3 of 10 agent packages. You get analysis data files, plots, a Jupyter notebook of the recorded steps, and lobster replay --verify with the verdicts MATCH, MISMATCH, NOT_COMPARED, REFUSED, NOTEBOOK_FAILED or MATCH_CUSTOM_POLICY. Also on your machine: the local project, a folder with a hidden .lobster_workspace; a local model such as Ollama, with which messages stay local too; and an optional LaminDB catalog, off by default. Over the network, the LLM provider you choose receives messages and tool results: Omics-OS Cloud (default), Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Azure AI, OpenRouter, Nebius AI Studio or Ollama Cloud. Agents use public data from GEO, SRA, PubMed and MetaboLights. Colour: red is the Lobster AI engine, teal genomics, purple proteomics, yellow-green transcriptomics and single-cell. Data, results and plumbing are grey.
